newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN GARDENS MINED TO BEAT CRIMEWAVE - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN GARDENS MINED TO BEAT CRIMEWAVE - PAPER.

text.p: South Africans battling to protect their property against stop-at-nothing criminals have taken to sowing landmines in their gardens, according to a man who says he's been selling the devices.

The Star newspaper quoted the unnamed "commodities dealer" as saying he had sold anti-personnel mines, including deadly Claymore fragmentation munitions, via the paper's own classified columns for $30 dollars each or less.

He claimed the mines, which buyers could plant at "strategic" sites in their gardens and backyards, were no threat to children or pets since in most cases they required pressure of 45 kg (100 pounds) or more to detonate.
The Star, a major daily dedicated to a crusade against South Africa's spreading crime wave, said it would refuse any further ads for landmines.
